newsitem.title: USA: Mass. business coalition decries EPA air proposals.
newsitem.headline: Mass. business coalition decries EPA air proposals.

text.p: A day before hearings are set begin on the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's proposed air emission standards, a coalition of Massachusetts industries on Monday said businesses would face huge, unnecessary costs if the such regulations were enforced.

Robert Ruddick, executive vice president of the week-old Massachusetts Clean Air Coalition, told reporters the proposed standards were "unrealistic" and would cost the petroleum, paper and transportation industries "tens of thousands of dollars" annually.

"Massachusetts was frankly on the verge of success. We were within a year of satisfying the current standards for the federal clean air act for ozone," Ruddick said. "Now frankly, the goal posts have been moved a great distance."

The proposed regulations aim to cut levels of ozone, or smog, by 30 percent and particulates, or soot, by 60 percent, said Peter Guldberg of Tech Environmental Inc of Waltham, Mass. Guldberg is a scientist who set to testify at the first of two hearings Tuesday in Boston on the proposed regulations.

The new standards, if put into effect, would likely require expensive gasoline reformulations, drive up utility costs and impose stricter controls on motorized vehicles, all without a scientific basis, Guldberg said.
"We've reached the margins of value." he said."EPA's proposed ozone standard is so low that even Mother Nature would violate it consistently."

The coalition consists of the Massachusetts Motor Tranportation Association, the Massachusetts Oil Heat Council, the Massachusetts Office of the American Automobile Manufacturers' Association, the state's Petroleum Council, the Printing Industries of New England and the New England Council.
